audit_findings.title: Company-owned life insurance could be purged asymmetrically
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 pretax: $120.3 million of policy investment and redemption income, $128.1 million of policy-loan interest and insurance costs, and $7.8 million net expense; the opposing gross amounts equal 17.8% and 19.0% of the $674.3 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: An asymmetric portfolio-income adjustment would directly alter anchor owner earnings and every scenario derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Income earned on our life insurance policies and redemptions, interest expense on borrowings against cash surrender values and cost of insurance charges are included in the Other (income) expense, net caption in the accompanying consolidated statements of income as follows (in millions):
audit_findings.explanation: No asymmetric adjustment is demonstrated because the anchor reconciliation was not supplied. However, the filed gross income and expense components are large relative to the anchor: retaining only the expenses would understate value, while retaining only the income would overstate value. The small $7.8 million net expense does not make a gross-side mismatch immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Produce the line-by-line 2025 owner-earnings reconciliation, including the $107.3 million investment income, $13.0 million redemption income, $109.3 million policy-loan interest, $18.8 million insurance cost, and associated tax effects; rerun if the components were not treated symmetrically.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may treat acquisition-funded growth as free
audit_findings.magnitude: $364.6 million of acquisition cash outflow in 2024, equal to 54.1% of the $674.3 million anchor; the future acquisition funding requirement is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth acquired with purchase consideration requires cash, debt service, or equity issuance not captured by ordinary property-and-equipment reinvestment, reducing owner earnings or increasing shares.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to continue growing our business through acquisitions and internal growth initiatives, particularly those that broaden our geographic footprint and processing capabilities in new and existing markets.
audit_findings.explanation: A modeling error is not yet demonstrated because the record does not identify how much of the 3% and 6% growth assumptions is organic. The company nevertheless expressly combines acquisitions with internal growth, and recent acquisition spending was large relative to anchor owner earnings. Because roughly 46%–52% of scenario value comes from terminal value, treating acquisition-supported growth as costless is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile projected growth to organic volume, pricing, capacity, and reinvestment already deducted from owner earnings. Rerun any scenario whose growth requires acquisitions using recurring acquisition consideration, incremental interest, or dilution.

audit_findings.title: The anchor embeds a large, potentially reversible LIFO charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $113.7 million 2025 pretax LIFO expense, equal to 16.9% of the $674.3 million anchor; $258.1 million pretax year-over-year swing; $150.0 million additional LIFO expense in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: The LIFO charge reduces reported earnings incorporated into anchor owner earnings; carrying, reversing, or normalizing it changes the starting OE and projected margins.
audit_findings.evidence: Our LIFO gross profit margin was 28.7% in 2025, down 100 basis points year-over-year, mainly due to a swing in LIFO inventory valuation adjustments—from $144.4 million of income in 2024 to $113.7 million of expense in 2025—driven in part by higher aluminum costs that had a disproportionate impact on LIFO expense.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge is filed and material in scale, but an error is not demonstrated. Reliance says LIFO reflects current replacement costs, and the additional $150.0 million expense in the first half of 2026 shows that the burden had not yet reversed. Permanently extrapolating a temporary reserve build could understate value, while removing an economically persistent replacement-cost effect could overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the LIFO adjustment through net income, inventory changes, and owner earnings, then rerun explicit carry-forward, stabilization, and reversal cases without treating a noncash reserve change itself as distributable cash.

audit_findings.title: A potentially significant multiemployer-plan claim is off balance sheet
audit_findings.mechanism: A withdrawal liability would be a senior claim against equity in the valuation bridge; ongoing contributions already reduce earnings, but the contingent withdrawal amount does not.
audit_findings.evidence: If we were to withdraw our participation from these plans, we would be required to recognize a liability on our balance sheet and the amount could be significant.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates exposure to endangered, critical, or critical-and-declining plans and reports $5.7 million of 2025 contributions, but it provides no withdrawal-liability estimate or evidence that withdrawal is probable. The possible claim could reduce equity value, yet the record cannot establish its size or present materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain each plan's funding notice, rehabilitation status, employer contribution history, and estimated withdrawal liability, and assess closure, restructuring, or withdrawal probability before adding a bridge claim or downside scenario.

audit_findings.title: Residual parent-versus-consolidated claim mismatch may remain
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.4 million NCI equity and $2.2 million 2025 NCI income; respectively 0.10% of the $9,709 million base equity value and 0.33% of the $674.3 million anchor, with the equity claim equal to about $0.18 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Using parent-attributable income with fully consolidated depreciation, capital expenditures, or cash flow could leave minority-owned cash flows in OE; an undeducted NCI claim would affect the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The ownership of the other interest holders of consolidated subsidiaries is reflected as noncontrolling interests.
audit_findings.explanation: The detailed adjustment alignment has not been demonstrated, so the residual mismatch should still be checked. The filed NCI claim and annual NCI earnings are nevertheless very small relative to both base equity value and anchor owner earnings, providing a concrete basis for concluding that the identified scale is not material to the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Verify that depreciation, capital expenditures, and other OE adjustments for the 56%- and 96%-owned subsidiaries are parent-attributable; rerun only if the resulting cash-flow mismatch materially exceeds the filed $2.2 million annual NCI earnings scale.
